records.title: Revealing the Challenges of Attention-FFN Disaggregation for Modern MoE Models and Hardware Systems
records.reason: The paper analyzes Attention-FFN Disaggregation (AFD) specifically for large MoE inference. It extends a roofline/HFU analysis with communication budget constraints, identifies conditions where network bandwidth or imbalance prevents AFD from improving utilization, and describes when Superpod-class interconnects and coarser, less sparse experts can benefit. It offers useful deployment guidance and an analysis method, but no new serving implementation or directly evaluated optimization, so it is retained as borderline for root review.

records.title: Predicting LLM Output Length via Entropy-Guided Representations
records.reason: EGTP/PLP predicts output lengths from internal model activations to support length-aware serving batches and reduce padding waste. In two vLLM serving workloads, the integrated scheduler reports throughput 131.05 versus 129.58 for the strongest listed baseline in Long Sequence and 194.21 versus 150.57 in Reasoning; padding ratios are 0.18 and 0.09. The authors report average predictor MAE reductions of 29.16% versus the strongest baseline and 55.09% versus SSJF-Reg. This directly evaluates inference-throughput scheduling.

records.title: HISA: Efficient Hierarchical Indexing for Fine-Grained Sparse Attention
records.reason: HISA replaces the exhaustive token indexer in sparse attention with two-stage hierarchical filtering, retaining the downstream token-index interface and requiring no additional training. End-to-end DeepSeek-V3.2 serving results report 1.65x throughput and 1.70x time-to-first-token improvements over the official DSA implementation. The paper also reports a quality/per-selection approximation boundary: token-set overlap falls to 78.66% at the longest evaluated positions, which should be covered in any later full summary.

records.title: Autopoiesis: A Self-Evolving System Paradigm for LLM Serving Under Runtime Dynamics
records.reason: Autopoiesis evolves LLM-serving policies as runtime workload and cluster conditions change. Across evaluated scenarios it reports up to 53% and average 34% improvement over state-of-the-art serving systems; in one elastic-cluster comparison it reports up to 53% and average 44% reduction in total execution time. The paper discusses LLM API cost/availability and deployment considerations. Direct serving-performance work.

records.title: CoLLM: Continuous Adaptation for SLO-Aware LLM Serving on Shared GPU Clusters
records.reason: CoLLM co-orchestrates LoRA fine-tuning with inference on shared GPU replicas to use idle compute while maintaining SLO-aware serving. On production-scale traces and GPU testbeds it reports up to 1.5x higher inference goodput, 2.2x quality-weighted goodput, and 40% improved GPU utilization versus state-of-the-art serving systems. Training is a system mechanism; the measured serving objective is inference goodput under SLOs.

records.title: Efficient Serving for Dynamic Agent Workflows with Prediction-based KV-Cache Management
records.reason: PBKV predicts multi-step agent calls and manages KV eviction/prefetch to raise cache reuse. It reports up to 1.85× lower average workflow latency versus LRU on dynamic workflows and up to 1.26× versus KVFlow on static workflows; cache hit-rate gains are up to 2.55× and 1.39×, respectively. Direct serving latency optimization through inference KV management.

records.title: Stateful Inference for Low-Latency Multi-Agent Tool Calling
records.reason: The paper preserves conversation KV state across multi-agent turns and processes only newly appended tokens, while adding scheduling, prefix sharing, and prompt-lookup speculation. Against vLLM and SGLang on novel workflows with response-cache hits excluded, it reports 2.1x lower median per-turn latency on a six-turn workflow and 4.2x lower median latency on a 35-turn workflow. This directly optimizes multi-agent LLM inference latency.

records.title: FoMoE: Breaking the Full-Replica Barrier with a Federation of MoEs
records.reason: The primary source states that FoMoE partitions expert layers across workers and skips non-resident experts during local training; its stated target is cross-site MoE training over constrained WAN links (abstract and §1). The reported communication reductions and skip-token throughput gains are training-system outcomes; §6 separates trained proxy quality runs and measured training throughput from modeled larger-scale results. §7 says XL/XXL and 100B-scale results are projections rather than end-to-end pretraining runs, and that the evaluation is controlled around homogeneous workers and synchronous rounds.

records.title: Gemma 4 Technical Report
records.reason: The report describes several concrete inference optimizations: local/global attention and KV sharing reduce global KV-cache footprint by up to 37.5%; an autoregressive multi-token-prediction head is released for speculative decoding; quantized checkpoints reduce parameter memory; and the 150M image encoder's W8A8 quantization halves forward-pass memory and reduces on-device latency by 44%. These are direct LLM/multimodal inference efficiency contributions, rather than only a model-capability report.

records.title: RAC: Reference-Aware Activation Compression for Communication-Efficient Split LLM Inference
records.reason: RAC compresses transient split-inference boundary activations using reference KV states and residual quantization. Across three models and nine model-link pairs, payload is reported at about 27.8% of raw for prefill and 25% for decode; mean TTFT speed ratios are 1.24-2.72x and TPOT ratios 1.01-2.79x. The paper also reports bandwidth-dependent crossover cases with latency regression, so the gains are conditional on link regime. The Edge / On-device LLM Systems destination is consistent with split/edge execution.

records.title: BALANCE: Hybrid Autoregressive-Speculative LLM Inference at the Network Edge
records.reason: BALANCE jointly schedules users and allocates compute/memory between autoregressive and speculative decoding at the edge under latency and memory constraints. It reports higher task throughput than conventional AD and SD; ablations report average gains up to 5.6%, 18.7% and 23.7% over equal-compute, equal-memory and equal-compute-and-memory variants, respectively. This directly targets resource-efficient edge LLM inference.

records.title: Governing the KV Cache: Preventing Timing Side-Channel Leakage in Multi-Tenant LLM Inference
records.reason: KVGov binds KV-cache keys to authenticated tenants to prevent prompt reconstruction through timing attacks; the paper reports HMAC salting reduces attack success to zero. Its primary objective is security, not inference efficiency. It nevertheless quantifies serving-path overhead (+1.3 microseconds per cache-key lookup) and lost cross-tenant prefix reuse, so it is closely related to KV-cache serving trade-offs but is only borderline for this inference-optimization collection.
